Where there's life, there's Mercy. 

Where there's care, there's You.

Through the battles and the breakthroughs, we're there. Where will you be?

For over a century, our incredible teams have provided care for people when they need it most. Our people feel great pride in this, and they value the security and stability we offer. But it also means so much opportunity - to build on all that's gone before, to grow your impact and gain experience that's hard to find elsewhere.

As a for-purpose organisation with over 10,000 dedicated, compassionate people, we continue to offer more services and deeper care than ever before. With Mercy, you'll have the chance to make an impact and gain experience that's hard to find elsewhere.

At Mercy Health, it's all about taking what we have and making it better. 

To do that, we need you. 

Join us at Mercy Health, and help our teams deliver even greater outcomes. 

About the opportunity

Our Birthing Suite midwives are highly skilled, and passionate about providing evidenced based, women centred care.

Work a rotating roster including Morning, Afternoon & Night duty shifts, with the opportunity to upskill and work 0930-1800 triaging induction bookings and performing cervical ripening for induction of labour. Should you prefer to work only night duty shifts, this will also be considered. 

We support our midwives to grow and develop their skills to be able to provide hollistic care in birthing services.

What you'll bring

You're resilient, compassionate and have a whole lot of heart. Most importantly, you are committed to delivering exceptional patient-centred care.

To thrive in this role, you will have:

Previous birthing suite experience

Level 2 or above RANZCOG practitioner status

Competence to perform IV Cannulation, Balloon Catheter insertion for induction of labour, perineal suturing, and waterbirth (or working towards these skills)

Knowledge of managing high risk, complicated pregnancies and birth, but also possess the skills and desire to facilitate physiological birth where possible

About you: 

You are approachable, compassionate and contribute to a positive team culture. 

Excellent clinical, time management, organisational and communication skills, with the ability to adapt and problem solve.

You are compassionate and demonstrate a flexible and positive approach to effective patient care

You will also be required to provide evidence of, or in the process of obtaining:

A current Police Record Check and Working with Children Check.

Proof of current influenza vaccination and other vaccination status consistent with public health orders.

AHPRA Registration

Ready to help us shape the future of healthcare?

Join us and make a meaningful difference in people's lives - and your career.

Are you ready to apply for this role? Click Apply now

Please contact us if you would like to find out more or communicate any requirements to ensure we provide you with a fair and equitable interview and selection process.

We acknowledge the Wurundjeri Woi-wurrung peoples, traditional Custodians of the Land in which our Head Office is based, on traditional lands of the Kulin Nation and recognise their deep connections to the land, sea, and culture.

We extend this acknowledgment to the many Traditional Lands that we operate across Australia and pay our respects to Elders past and present.

The team at Mercy Health is as wonderfully diverse as the patients, residents, clients and communities we support. We're proud to be recognised as an Employer of Choice for Gender Equality by the Workplace Gender Equality Agency (WGEA). ## Telecommunications Technical Officer / Technologist
## Position Overview
We are looking for a skilled and detail-oriented Telecommunications Technical Officer or Technologist to join our team and contribute to the delivery of reliable, high-performance telecommunications infrastructure. This role is responsible for the design, installation, maintenance, and optimisation of complex communication networks and systems across a range of technologies. The ideal candidate brings solid hands-on technical experience, strong analytical capability, and the ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment. This position suits a proactive professional who is committed to maintaining the highest standards of network performance and service delivery.
## Key Responsibilities
- Install, configure, and maintain microwave, satellite, telemetry, and other radio and electromagnetic communication systems, ensuring all equipment operates to specification and within regulatory requirements.
- Diagnose, troubleshoot, and resolve network faults, performance issues, and equipment malfunctions in a timely and effective manner, minimising disruption to services.
- Integrate telecommunications networks with computer hardware, software platforms, operating systems, databases, and peripheral devices to ensure seamless end-to-end functionality.
- Monitor the ongoing performance of complex networks and communication systems, identifying trends, anomalies, and areas for optimisation before they impact service quality.
- Plan and support the development of customer access network infrastructure, contributing to capacity planning, design reviews, and upgrade programmes.
- Maintain accurate and up-to-date documentation including inventory logs, equipment records, asset statuses, and communication policies, procedures, and quality standards in accordance with organisational and regulatory guidelines.
- Provide clear technical advice and support to internal stakeholders, project teams, and end users on telecommunications systems, configurations, and best practices.
- Liaise with vendors, suppliers, and external service providers to coordinate procurement, installation activities, and ongoing service delivery, whilst monitoring contractual performance and obligations.
- Support the design and optimisation of network architecture, contributing technical input to projects aimed at improving reliability, scalability, and performance.
- Conduct routine inspections, preventive maintenance, and equipment testing to ensure network integrity and compliance with applicable standards.
- Assist in the development and review of technical documentation, including network diagrams, standard operating procedures, and incident reports.
- Collaborate with cross-functional teams on telecommunications projects, providing technical expertise throughout the project lifecycle from scoping through to commissioning and handover.
## Required Qualifications & Skills
- A diploma, advanced diploma, or bachelor's degree in Telecommunications Engineering, Electronics, Information Technology, or a related field; or equivalent industry experience in lieu of formal qualifications.
- Demonstrated experience in a telecommunications technical role, with hands-on exposure to radio frequency (RF), microwave, satellite, or fixed-line communication systems.
- Solid understanding of network protocols, telecommunications standards, and systems integration principles.
- Proficiency in configuring and troubleshooting network hardware, software, and associated technologies including switches, routers, and transmission equipment.
- Experience with network monitoring tools and fault management systems, with the ability to interpret performance data and take corrective action.
- Strong documentation skills with the ability to maintain accurate records, produce technical reports, and adhere to quality and compliance standards.
- Effective communication skills, with the ability to convey technical information clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
- Ability to manage competing priorities, work methodically under pressure, and deliver outcomes within agreed timeframes.
- A valid Australian driver's licence, as field-based work and site visits may be required.
- Willingness to participate in an on-call roster or undertake out-of-hours work when operational requirements demand.
## Preferred Qualifications
- Relevant industry certifications such as Cisco CCNA/CCNP, CompTIA Network+, or equivalent telecommunications qualifications.
- Experience working with microwave backhaul systems, fibre optic networks, or mobile network infrastructure (2G/3G/4G/5G).
- Familiarity with Australian telecommunications regulatory frameworks and compliance requirements, including those governed by the ACMA.
- Exposure to project management methodologies and experience contributing to telecommunications infrastructure projects.
- Knowledge of ITIL frameworks or experience working within a managed services or enterprise network environment.
- Postgraduate qualifications in Telecommunications, Network Engineering, or a related discipline.
## Why Join Us?
- Be part of a collaborative and highly skilled engineering team working on critical telecommunications infrastructure that makes a real difference to communities and businesses across Australia.
- Enjoy genuine opportunities for professional development, including access to industry training, certifications, and career progression pathways within the organisation.
- Benefit from a flexible working environment that supports work-life balance, with options for hybrid arrangements where operational requirements allow.
- Receive a competitive remuneration package with superannuation contributions, and access to additional employee benefits including wellness programmes and paid leave entitlements.
- Work on a diverse range of projects and technologies that will broaden your technical expertise and keep you at the forefront of the evolving telecommunications landscape.
## Job Details
- Job Type: Full-time, Permanent
- Work Schedule: 8-hour shift
- Salary: $70,000 – $120,000 per year + Superannuation

Location: Zuccoli / Darwin, Northern Territory
Employment Type: Full-time
Salary: $67,510 per annum plus superannuation

About Us
Skills and Hands NT Pty Ltd is a Northern Territory-based consultancy focused on workforce planning, talent engagement, and sustainable staffing strategies. We work alongside local businesses to support the development of strong, reliable teams through tailored pathways that align with their long-term goals. Our role is to facilitate practical workforce solutions that help employers attract and retain skilled talent—contributing to the resilience and continuity of operations across the Territory.

About the Employer
We are supporting a care services provider based in Darwin and surrounding areas, operating in the aged care, disability support, and community services sector. The business is known for its commitment to compassionate, respectful, and person-centred care, supporting clients to maintain their dignity, independence, wellbeing, and quality of life. With a growing team and services delivered across multiple client locations, they are seeking to fill the role of Aged or Disabled Carer. This opportunity offers stable employment, meaningful hands-on care work, and the chance to be part of a supportive and inclusive work environment focused on making a positive difference in people’s lives.

About the Role
As an Aged or Disabled Carer, you will provide practical and emotional support to clients who are aged, living with disability, or require assistance with daily activities. The role requires patience, respect, strong communication skills, and a genuine commitment to improving the quality of life of vulnerable clients.

Key Responsibilities
The successful applicant will be responsible for:
- Providing personal care support, including hygiene, grooming, dressing, toileting, and mobility assistance
- Supporting clients with daily living activities in their home and community
- Assisting with meal preparation, feeding support, and basic household tasks
- Supporting clients to attend appointments, social activities, and community participation
- Monitoring client wellbeing and reporting any changes, concerns, incidents, or risks to the supervisor
- Providing companionship and emotional support in a respectful and professional manner
- Following individual care plans, workplace policies, and NDIS-related requirements
- Maintaining accurate records, progress notes, and communication with relevant team members
- Assisting with safe manual handling and mobility support, where required
- Promoting client independence, dignity, choice, and privacy at all times

Selection Criteria
Applicants should be able to demonstrate:
1. Experience providing care or support to aged persons, people with disability, or vulnerable clients
2. A caring, patient, respectful, and reliable approach to client support
3. Good communication skills and ability to follow care instructions
4. Ability to assist with personal care and daily living tasks
5. Understanding of confidentiality, duty of care, and client dignity
6. Ability to work independently and as part of a small care team
7. Flexibility to work across different shifts, including weekends where required
8. Commitment to safe work practices, infection control, and client wellbeing

Required Experience and Qualifications
- Minimum 1–2 years of relevant care/support experience preferred
- Relevant qualification in aged care, disability support, individual support, community services, or similar field is preferred but not mandatory
- Current First Aid and CPR certificate, or willingness to obtain
- NDIS Worker Screening Check, or willingness to obtain
- National Police Check, or willingness to obtain
- Driver licence and access to reliable transport is preferred
- Full working rights in Australia

How to Apply
We are looking for a compassionate, reliable, and safety-minded Aged or Disabled Carer to support clients with daily living activities and help promote their independence, dignity, wellbeing, and quality of life.

To apply, please submit the following:
- Resume outlining your work experience and references.
- A short cover letter of no more than 300 words explaining:
- Why you are applying for this position; and
- An example of when you showed excellent service, initiative, or teamwork. Please use the STAR method: Situation, Task, Action,
Result.
- A written response of no more than 600 words describing how your skills and experience align with the responsibilities of the role. Please structure your example or examples using the STAR method.

* Only complete applications that address all three components will be considered. Incomplete or generic submissions will not be shortlisted.

If you are interested in joining a caring and supportive community services business that values compassion, respect, safety, dignity, and person-centred care, we look forward to receiving your application.

Apply online only. Phone calls and walk-in applications will not be accepted.

Applications close: 04 August 2026

result.description:
Objective
To be a key member of the Mission to Seafarers South Australia team, providing welfare services to visiting seafarers while supporting the sustainable development and operation of Mission to Seafarers centres across South Australia.
Based in Port Pirie, the Port Welfare Officers will share responsibility for providing seafarer welfare services, supporting volunteers and committees, coordinating administration, and assisting with the development of services in all South Australian ports, including Port Adelaide,  Port Lincoln, Port Giles, Thevenard, Wallaroo and any future centres established within the state.
The role combines practical seafarer welfare, volunteer coordination, administration, stakeholder engagement and centre development.

Level of Responsibility
The Port Welfare Officers report directly to the Regional Director, Mission to Seafarers Australia.
They work closely with the South Australian Management Committee, local port committees, volunteers, port authorities, shipping agents, churches and other stakeholders to ensure effective delivery of welfare services throughout the state.

The role shares responsibility for:
Day-to-day operation of the Port Pirie Seafarers Centre.
Development and support of Mission to Seafarers activities throughout South Australia.
Volunteer recruitment, training and support.
Administrative and financial management of the South Australian operations.
Regular travel to South Australian ports to visit ships, support volunteers and strengthen relationships with industry partners.

Conditions
The successful applicant will be required to maintain:
Current Driver's Licence.
National Police Check.
Safe Church Communities accreditation (or equivalent).
Working With Children Check (or applicable state screening requirements).
Australian Border Force and Port Security access requirements as required.
Capacity to travel throughout South Australia, including overnight travel where necessary.

About the Role
This position would suit someone who is passionate about improving the welfare of seafarers, enjoys working with volunteers and industry, is highly organised, flexible and self-motivated, and is comfortable working across multiple locations.
The role requires initiative, strong communication skills and the ability to build relationships with maritime industry stakeholders while developing sustainable welfare services across regional ports.

Knowledge and Experience
The successful applicant will possess excellent interpersonal and communication skills together with confidence using technology.
A sound working knowledge of Microsoft Office, Xero or similar accounting software, databases, social media and web-based systems is desirable.

Essential Skills and Experience
Office administration experience.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Strong organisational and time management skills.
Ability to work independently and as part of a small team.
Proficient in Microsoft Office.
Experience using accounting software (preferably Xero).
Experience coordinating volunteers or community programs.
Current driver's licence and willingness to travel.
Desirable Skills and Experience
Experience preparing agendas, minutes and financial reports.
Website and social media management.
Marketing and communications experience.
Fundraising and grant administration.
Community development experience.
Understanding of the Mission to Seafarers and the maritime industry.
Experience working with committees or not-for-profit organisations.

Duties and Responsibilities
1. Seafarer Welfare
Visit ships and provide welfare support to visiting seafarers.
Coordinate transport, shopping, communications and welfare services.
Supply SIM cards, Wi-Fi access and welfare items.
Assist with emergency welfare situations when required.
Promote compliance with the Maritime Labour Convention welfare provisions.
2. Centre and Port Development
Support the ongoing development of Mission to Seafarers services throughout South Australia.
Assist with establishing and growing welfare activities in new and developing ports.
Identify opportunities to improve facilities and services.
Build relationships with port authorities, shipping agents, terminal operators and industry stakeholders.
Promote awareness of seafarer welfare across the maritime community.
3. Administration
Prepare agendas, reports and committee meeting minutes.
Complete and maintain Australian Border Force documentation.
Maintain registrations, licences and compliance records.
Monitor donations and acknowledge supporters.
Support committee office bearers with administration.
Manage SIM cards, vouchers and foreign currency.
Assist the Regional Director with reporting and projects.
4. Communications and Marketing
Monitor incoming enquiries.
Coordinate communications with volunteers, shipping agents and port stakeholders.
Maintain websites and social media platforms.
Produce promotional material highlighting Mission activities.
Represent Mission to Seafarers at community and industry events.
5. Volunteer Management
Recruit new volunteers across South Australia.
Coordinate induction, training and mentoring.
Maintain volunteer records and compliance.
Coordinate Working With Children Checks, port inductions, First Aid and other required training.
Develop volunteer rosters where applicable.
6. Financial Administration
Assist with day-to-day financial administration.
Process invoices and expenses.
Support budgeting and financial reporting.
Maintain accurate records using Xero or equivalent systems.
7. Stakeholder Engagement
Develop productive relationships with:
Flinders Ports
Shipping agents
Maritime unions
AMSA
Australian Border Force
Port Welfare Committees
Local churches
Community organisations
Government agencies
Represent Mission to Seafarers at meetings and forums as required.
8. Attendance
Attend:
South Australian committee meetings.
National Mission to Seafarers conferences.
Volunteer training events.
Industry meetings and conferences.
Ship visits across South Australian ports.
Other duties as directed by the Regional Director.

Employment Conditions
The position is offered as a job-share arrangement, with two Port Welfare Officers working collaboratively to provide consistent coverage across South Australia.
The combined role is funded at 5Days per week, with flexibility to increase hours through project funding or centre development initiatives.
Regular travel throughout South Australia is an essential component of the role, with a Mission vehicle available where appropriate.
Comprehensive on-the-job training will be provided.
The role would suit someone with several years of workplace experience who enjoys working with people, is comfortable travelling, and wants to make a meaningful contribution to the wellbeing of international seafarers visiting South Australian ports.

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Advance your nursing career in a highly specialised and rewarding clinical role.

Employment Type: Temporary Part Time until January 2027
Position Classification: Clinical Nurse Specialist Grade 2
Remuneration: $58.83 - $60.76 + 12% Superannuation + Salary Packaging 
Hours Per Week: 28
Requisition ID: REQ676271
Located in: Armidale Hospital

Closing Date: Sunday 12th July 2026 

About the Opportunity

An exciting temporary part-time opportunity is available for an experienced and compassionate Clinical Nurse Specialist (CNS) to join the Acute Pain Service (APS). Working within a multidisciplinary team, you will deliver evidence-based pain management care to patients across a complex acute care setting.
The Acute Pain Service is committed to providing high-quality, patient-centred care while supporting contemporary clinical practice and professional collaboration. You will be supported by the Deputy Director of Nursing and Midwifery and have access to ongoing professional development and mentorship to help you succeed in the role.

What You Will Be Doing

In this role within the Acute Pain Service, you will provide safe, evidence-based and person-centred care to patients experiencing acute and chronic non-cancer pain. Working within a multidisciplinary team, you will collaborate with patients, families and carers to support effective pain management and achieve optimal health outcomes.

You will deliver specialist acute pain management across a diverse clinical setting, including elective and emergency surgical patients, trauma presentations from the Emergency Department, and referrals from specialty units across the hospital.
This role offers the opportunity to apply advanced clinical expertise in a complex and dynamic environment while contributing to high-quality, coordinated and patient-focused care. You will report to the Deputy Director of Nursing and Midwifery and be supported within a strong culture of collaboration and clinical excellence.

About you

You are a compassionate and motivated clinician committed to delivering high-quality, evidence-based, person-centred care. You thrive in a collaborative multidisciplinary team, demonstrate sound clinical judgement, and are passionate about improving patient outcomes through clinical excellence.

Essential requirements:

 Current Authority to Practice as a Registered Nurse with AHPRA with relevant post-registration qualifications and at least 3 years' experience working in pain management of their specified post-graduate qualification, or such other qualifications or equivalent experience deemed appropriate by the public hospital or public health organisation. 
 Demonstrated clinical knowledge and experience in pain management 
 Strong communication and interpersonal skills
 The ability to work collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team
 Excellent clinical reasoning and problem-solving skills
 A compassionate and patient-centred approach to care delivery

What we can offer you:

 Temporary accommodation if relocating 
 Access to the Welcome experience to welcome you into the community 
 Opportunities for ongoing learning and professional development
 Sustainable Healthcare: Together towards zero
 Monthly Allocated Days Off (for full-time employees)
 4 weeks annual leave (pro-rata for part-time employees)
 Salary packaging options - up to $11,600 plus novated leasing
 Fitness Passport for health and well-being - discounted gym options for you and your family
 Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for staff and family members

Need more information? 
 1) Click here for the Position Description
 2) Find out more about applying for this position
For role related queries or questions contact John Kim on JaeHong.Kim@health.nsw.gov.au

Additional Information

To be eligible for permanent employment in this position you must be an Australian Citizen, or a permanent resident of Australia, or a New Zealand citizen with a current New Zealand Passport. Employment of a temporary visa holder may only occur if no suitable local candidate is identified for the position; in this instance, you may only be offered employment in line with the conditions and expiry date of your visa.

We are unable to accommodate visa sponsorship for applicants requiring a visa for this position. 

An eligibility list will be created for future temporary full or part time vacancies

Hunter New England Health is dedicated to fostering a child-safe environment that respects and upholds the rights of children and young people, aligned with NSW Health's commitment to implementing the Child Safe Standards. We aim to ensure that children and young people feel safe, supported, and included in their care. All current and prospective staff are expected to prioritise the safety, welfare, and well-being of children and young people, actively working to protect them from harm and abuse.

At Hunter New England Local Health District, we are an inclusive employer dedicated to fostering a diverse, inclusive, and welcoming workplace. Our commitment to a workforce that reflects the community we care for is essential for delivering the highest quality healthcare to our community. We encourage people with diverse lived experiences to apply. If you require any accommodations or adjustments to the recruitment process please let us know when you apply or at any stage of the process. We will work with you to meet your needs and create the best possible experience. Please contact HNELHD-Diversity@health.nsw.gov.au for confidential support.

Information for Applicants:

Applicants will be assessed against the essential requirements and selection criteria contained within the position description (link below). For assistance addressing selection criteria visit: https:--bit.ly-3vL5fq2

Stepping Up Website is a resource designed to help indigenous job applicants apply for positions in NSW Health. For more information, please visit: https:--bit.ly-HNEHealthSteppingUp

This is a Category A position. Recommended applicants will be reviewed for compliance with NSW Health policy directive PD2024_015: Occupational Assessment, Screening and Vaccination against Specified Infectious Diseases for Category A positions prior to offer. All new employees must agree to comply with the requirements outlined in the policy.

Salary Packaging: is beneficial to most Hunter New England Health employees and may increase your take-home pay! Salary package a range of personal expenses including novated motor vehicle leases, relocation expenses, and HECS-HELP debt. Find out more by contacting SalaryPackagingPLUS! via nswhealth@salarypackagingplus.com.au or 1300 40 25 23.

Hunter New England Health employees may be eligible for a range of benefits such as allocated days off (ADO) for full time employees, long service leave, paid maternity leave, and salary packaging options including meal expenses.

CHEF – Full-Time Position
PBUP PTY LTD T/A Dhamaka Indian Restaurant & Bar
Location - Caboolture QLD 4510
Salary: $79,000 – $89,000 per year
Employment Type: Full-time, Permanent
Work Location: In person

About Us

PBUP PTY LTD, trading as Dhamaka Indian Restaurant & Bar, is a vibrant and highly regarded dining
destination located in the heart of Caboolture QLD 4510. We are known for delivering authentic
Indian cuisine crafted with locally sourced produce and premium spices. Our diverse menu includes
vegetarian, vegan, and allergen-sensitive options, reflecting our commitment to providing
exceptional dining experiences for every guest.

The Opportunity

We are currently seeking a skilled and passionate Chef to join our dynamic team on a full-time basis.
This is an exciting opportunity for a culinary professional who takes pride in delivering high-quality
dishes and contributing to a positive and efficient kitchen environment.

Key Responsibilities

• Develop and plan menus, forecast ingredient requirements, and manage food and labour
costs.
• Ensure consistent quality in food preparation, cooking, and presentation.
• Liaise with management, dietitians, kitchen staff, and service teams regarding food
preparation and operational requirements.
• Demonstrate cooking techniques and provide guidance and training to kitchen staff.
• Prepare and cook a wide range of dishes in line with established recipes and quality
standards.
• Maintain high standards of hygiene, food safety, and kitchen sanitation practices.
• Assist in recruiting, selecting, and training kitchen staff as required.
• Store, preserve, and freeze food items appropriately to maintain quality and minimise waste.
• Oversee daily kitchen operations to ensure smooth workflow and timely service delivery.

Qualifications & Experience

• AQF Associate Degree, Advanced Diploma, or Diploma in Culinary Arts or a related field.
• Minimum of 1 year of experience in a commercial kitchen or food service environment.
• Strong knowledge of food safety regulations and kitchen operations.
• Excellent leadership, teamwork, and time management skills.
• Creative flair and a genuine passion for cooking.

What We Offer

• Competitive annual salary ranging from $79,000 to $89,000 based on experience and skills.
• Opportunities for career progression and professional development.
• A supportive, inclusive, and friendly workplace culture.
• Employee discounts on meals.
• A platform to showcase your culinary creativity in a dynamic restaurant environment.

How to Apply

If you are passionate about cooking and ready to contribute your skills and creativity to our team, we
would love to hear from you.

Please submit your resume outlining why you are the ideal candidate for the Chef position at PBUP PTY LTD T/A Dhamaka Indian Restaurant & Bar.

Join us and be part of a team dedicated to delivering exceptional Indian cuisine and memorable
dining experiences.
